metadata.title: A unifying view on implicit bias in training linear neural networks
metadata.authors: Chulhee Yun, Shankar Krishnan, Hossein Mobahi

nodes.name: Multilinear multiplication
nodes.statement: Given a tensor $\tA \in \reals^{k_1 \times \cdots \times k_L}$ and linear maps $\mB_l \in \reals^{p_l \times k_l}$, the multilinear product is $\tA \circ (\mB_1^T,\dots,\mB_L^T) \defeq \sum_{j_1,\dots,j_L} [\tA]_{j_1,\dots,j_L} (\mB_1 \ve^{k_1}_{j_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes \mB_L \ve^{k_L}_{j_L}) \in \reals^{p_1\times \cdots \times p_L}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Multilinear product between an order-L tensor and L linear maps, generalizing left/right matrix multiplication.

nodes.name: Tensor formulation of neural network
nodes.statement: Given $\vx \in \reals^d$ and linear data map $\tM(\vx) \in \reals^{k_1 \times \cdots \times k_L}$, the network with parameters $\vv_l \in \reals^{k_l}$ and activation $\phi$ computes $\tH_l(\vx) = \phi(\tH_{l-1}(\vx) \circ (\vv_l, \mI_{k_{l+1}},\dots,\mI_{k_L}))$ and $f(\vx;\bTheta)=\tH_{L-1}(\vx)\circ \vv_L$.
nodes.statement_clean: General tensor representation of an L-layer network: layers act as multilinear contractions of a data tensor with parameter vectors.

nodes.name: Diagonal network
nodes.statement: An $L$-layer diagonal network is $\fdiag(\vx;\bThetadiag) = \phi(\cdots \phi(\phi(\vx \odot \vw_1) \odot \vw_2)\cdots \odot \vw_{L-1})^T \vw_L$, with $\vw_l \in \reals^d$. It corresponds to the tensor form with $[\tMdiag(\vx)]_{j,j,\dots,j}=[\vx]_j$ and zero otherwise.
nodes.statement_clean: Network whose hidden layers act element-wise via Hadamard products with weight vectors.

nodes.name: Circular convolutional network
nodes.statement: An $L$-layer circular convolutional network is $\fconv(\vx;\bThetaconv)=\phi(\cdots \phi(\phi(\vx \star \vw_1)\star \vw_2)\cdots \star \vw_{L-1})^T \vw_L$, with $[\va\star\vb]_i=\sum_{j=1}^k [\va]_{(i+j-1)\bmod d}[\vb]_j$ and data tensor $[\tMconv(\vx)]_{j_1,\dots,j_L}=[\vx]_{(\sum_l j_l-L+1) \bmod d}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Network with circular convolutions across $L-1$ layers and a final fully-connected layer.

nodes.name: Fully-connected network
nodes.statement: An $L$-layer fully-connected network $\ffc(\vx;\bThetafc)=\phi(\cdots\phi(\phi(\vx^T \mW_1)\mW_2)\cdots \mW_{L-1})\vw_L$ with $\mW_l \in \reals^{d_l\times d_{l+1}}$. In tensor form, $\vv_l = \vect(\mW_l)$ and $\tMfc(\vx)$ is built recursively in a block-diagonal manner.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard MLP architecture, encoded into the tensor formulation via block-diagonal data tensors.

nodes.name: Linear tensor network
nodes.statement: A linear tensor network is the tensor formulation \eqref{eq:tensorrep} with linear activation $\phi(t)=t$, giving $f(\vx;\bTheta)=\tM(\vx)\circ(\vv_1,\dots,\vv_L)$. Equivalently $f(\vx;\bTheta)=\vx^T\vbeta(\bTheta)$ for some linear coefficient vector $\vbeta(\bTheta)\in\reals^d$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear-activation special case of the tensor formulation; reduces to a linear function $\vx^T \vbeta$ but with multilinear parameter dependence.

nodes.name: Singular vectors of a tensor
nodes.statement: For an order-$L$ tensor $\tA \in \reals^{k_1\times\cdots\times k_L}$, vectors $\vu_1,\dots,\vu_L$ and scalar $s$ are singular vectors and singular value if $s\vu_l = \tA \circ (\vu_1,\dots,\vu_{l-1},\mI_{k_l},\vu_{l+1},\dots,\vu_L)$ for all $l \in [L]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalization of matrix singular value decomposition to higher-order tensors due to Lim (2005).

nodes.name: Even vector
nodes.statement: A vector $\vx \in \reals^d$ is \emph{even} if $[\vx]_{j+2}=[\vx]_{d-j}$ for $j=0,\dots,\lfloor (d-3)/2 \rfloor$, i.e., even symmetry around the origin $[\vx]_1$. If $\vx$ is real and even, so is its DFT $\mF\vx$.
nodes.statement_clean: Notion of even symmetry for discrete vectors used in convolutional regression corollary.

nodes.name: Orthogonally decomposable data tensor
nodes.statement: There exist a full column-rank $\mS \in \C^{m\times d}$ ($d \leq m \leq \min_l k_l$) and matrices $\mU_l \in \C^{k_l\times m}$ with $\mU_l^H\mU_l=\mI_m$ such that $\tM(\vx)=\sum_{j=1}^m [\mS\vx]_j ([\mU_1]_{\cdot,j}\otimes\cdots\otimes [\mU_L]_{\cdot,j})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standing assumption that the data tensor admits an orthogonal CP-style decomposition with $\vx$-independent factors and singular values linear in $\vx$.

nodes.name: Separable binary classification with linear tensor network
nodes.statement: Given separable data $\{(\vx_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ with $y_i\in\{\pm1\}$, minimize $\mc L(\bTheta)=\sum_{i=1}^n \exp(-y_i f(\vx_i;\bTheta))$ over network parameters via gradient flow $\dot\bTheta = -\nabla_\bTheta \mc L(\bTheta)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Train a linear tensor network on linearly separable data using gradient flow on the exponential loss.

nodes.name: Underdetermined linear regression with linear tensor network
nodes.statement: Given data $\{(\vx_i,y_i)\}$ with $n\leq d$ and full row-rank $\mX$, minimize $\mc L(\bTheta)=\half\sum_{i=1}^n (f(\vx_i;\bTheta)-y_i)^2$ via gradient flow on the network parameters.
nodes.statement_clean: Train a linear tensor network on an underdetermined regression problem using gradient flow on the squared loss.

nodes.name: $\ell_2$ max-margin SVM
nodes.statement: $\minimize_{\vz\in\reals^d}\norm{\vz}\;\subjectto\; y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1,\ i\in[n]$, with $\ell_2$ norm in the cost.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard hard-margin SVM problem; baseline against which implicit-bias limit directions are compared.

nodes.name: Deep matrix sensing problem
nodes.statement: $\minimize_{\mW_1,\dots,\mW_L \in \reals^{d\times d}} \mc L_{\rm ms}(\mW_1\cdots\mW_L) \defeq \sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - \langle \mA_i, \mW_1\cdots\mW_L\rangle)^2$ with symmetric commuting sensor matrices $\mA_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize squared loss for matrix sensing with depth-$L$ matrix factorization parameterization.
nodes.origin_citation: Gunasekar et al. 2017; Arora et al. 2019

nodes.name: Gradient flow for linear tensor network parameters
nodes.statement: $\dot\vv_l = \tM(-\mX^T\vr) \circ (\vv_1,\dots,\vv_{l-1},\mI_{k_l},\vv_{l+1},\dots,\vv_L)$ for $l\in[L]$, with residual $[\vr]_i = -y_i \exp(-y_i f(\vx_i;\bTheta))$ for classification or $f(\vx_i;\bTheta)-y_i$ for regression, and initialization $\vv_l(0)=\alpha\bar\vv_l$.
nodes.statement_clean: ODE governing gradient flow on parameters of the linear tensor network.

nodes.name: Limit directions are tensor singular vectors
nodes.statement: If $\mc L(\bTheta(t_0))<1$ for some $t_0\geq 0$ and $\mX^T\vr(t)$ converges in direction to $\vu^\infty$, then $\vv_1,\dots,\vv_L$ converge in direction to singular vectors of $\tM(-\vu^\infty)$.
conclusions: $\vv_1,\dots,\vv_L$ converge in direction to singular vectors of $\tM(-\vu^\infty)$

nodes.name: Limit directions in orthogonally decomposable networks (classification)
nodes.statement: Under Assumption~\ref{assm:complex-diag-decomp}, if $|[\mU_l^T\bar\vv_l]_j|^2 - |[\mU_L^T\bar\vv_L]_j|^2 \geq \lambda$ for all $l\in[L-1], j\in[m]$, then $\mc L(\bTheta(t))\to 0$. If additionally $\mX^T\vr(t)$ converges in direction, $\vbeta(\bTheta(t))$ aligns with $\mS^T\vrho^\infty$ where $\vrho^\infty$ is a stationary point of $\min_{\vrho} \norms{\vrho}_{2/L}$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\mS^T\vrho \geq 1$.
conclusions: $\vbeta(\bTheta(t))$ aligns with $\mS^T\vrho^\infty$ for $\vrho^\infty$ stationary point of $\min_{\vrho\in\C^m} \norms{\vrho}_{2/L}$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\mS^T\vrho \geq 1$
If $\mS$ invertible: $\vbeta(\bTheta(t))$ aligns with stationary point of $\min_{\vz} \norms{\mS^{-T}\vz}_{2/L}$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1$

nodes.name: Limit directions in extremely overparameterized 2-layer networks (classification)
nodes.statement: For a 2-layer linear tensor network with single data point $(\vx,y)$ and SVD $\tM(\vx)=\mU_1\diag(\vs)\mU_2^T$, if $[\mU_1^T\bar\vv_1]_j^2 - [\mU_2^T\bar\vv_2]_j^2 \geq \lambda > 0$ for all $j\in[m]$, then $\mc L\to 0$ and $\vv_l$ converge to $\mU_l\veta_l^\infty$, with $|\veta_1^\infty|=|\veta_2^\infty|=|\vrho^\infty|^{\odot 1/2}$ for $\vrho^\infty$ minimizing $\norm{\vrho}_1$ s.t. $y\vs^T\vrho\geq 1$.

nodes.name: Limit point characterization in orthogonally decomposable networks (regression)
nodes.statement: Under Assumption~\ref{assm:complex-diag-decomp} with real $\mS,\mU_l$, choose $\bar\veta$ with $[\bar\veta]_j^2\geq \lambda>0$ and $\bar\vv_l = \mU_l\bar\veta$ for $l\in[L-1]$, $\bar\vv_L=\zeros$. Then $\vbeta(\bTheta(t))\to \mS^T\vrho^\infty$ where $\vrho^\infty$ minimizes $Q_{L,\alpha,\bar\veta}(\vrho)\defeq\alpha^2\sum_{j=1}^m [\bar\veta]_j^2 H_L\big(\frac{[\vrho]_j}{\alpha^L|[\bar\veta]_j|^L}\big)$ s.t. $\mX\mS^T\vrho=\vy$.

nodes.name: Limit points in extremely overparameterized 2-layer networks (regression)
nodes.statement:
For 2-layer linear tensor network with one data point and compact SVD $	M(\vx)=\mU_1\diag(\vs)\mU_2^T$, under the same gap condition, gradient flow converges and $\vv_l(t)$ converge to closed-form limits expressed via $\sinh,\cosh$ of $g^{-1}(y/\alpha^2)\vs$, with $g(
u)=\sum_j [\vs]_j(	frac{[\mU_1^T ar\vv_1]_j^2+[\mU_2^T ar\vv_2]_j^2}{2}\sinh(2[\vs]_j
u)+[\mU_1^T ar\vv_1]_j[\mU_2^T ar\vv_2]_j\cosh(2[\vs]_j
u))$.
conclusions: Gradient flow converges to a global minimizer of $\mc L$
$\vv_1^\infty, \vv_2^\infty$ given by closed-form expressions involving $\sinh, \cosh$ of $g^{-1}(y/\alpha^2)\vs$
As $\alpha\to 0$, top singular vectors dominate the limit points

nodes.name: Implicit bias of fully-connected networks in regression
nodes.statement: For an $L$-layer linear fully-connected network: (1) if $\bar\mW_l^T\bar\mW_l \succeq \bar\mW_{l+1}\bar\mW_{l+1}^T$ for $l\in[L-2]$ and $\bar\mW_{L-1}^T\bar\mW_{L-1}-\bar\vw_L\bar\vw_L^T \succeq \lambda \mI_d$, then $\mc L\to 0$; (2) if $\mc L\to 0$, then $\lim_{\alpha\to 0}\lim_{t\to\infty}\vbetafc(\bThetafc(t)) = \mX^T(\mX\mX^T)^{-1}\vy$.

nodes.name: ODE for $h_L$ function
nodes.statement: The system $\dot p = p^{L-2}q,\ \dot q = p^{L-1},\ p(0)=1,\ q(0)=0$ has continuous solutions $p_L,q_L$ on $(-c,c)$. Defining $h_L(t)=p_L(t)^{L-1}q_L(t)$, $h_L$ is odd, strictly increasing, and $\lim_{t\uparrow c} h_L(t)=\infty$, $\lim_{t\downarrow -c} h_L(t)=-\infty$.
assumptions: Initial value problem $\dot p = p^{L-2}q$, $\dot q = p^{L-1}$ with $p(0)=1, q(0)=0$
conclusions: Solutions $p_L(t), q_L(t)$ continuous on maximal interval $(-c,c)$, $c\in(0,\infty]$
$h_L(t) = p_L(t)^{L-1}q_L(t)$ is odd and strictly increasing

nodes.name: Linear fully-connected networks converge to $\ell_2$ max-margin (classification)
nodes.statement: If $\mc L(\bThetafc(t_0))<1$, then $\vbetafc(\bThetafc(t))$ converges in direction to the solution of $\min_{\vz}\ltwo{\vz}^2$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1, i\in[n]$.
conclusions: $\vbetafc(\bThetafc(t))$ converges in direction to the $\ell_2$ max-margin classifier $\arg\min_{\vz}\ltwo{\vz}^2$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1$

nodes.name: Diagonal networks converge to $\ell_{2/L}$ max-margin (classification)
nodes.statement: For an $L$-layer linear diagonal network, if $[\bar\vw_l]_j^2-[\bar\vw_L]_j^2\geq\lambda$ for $l\in[L-1], j\in[d]$ then $\mc L\to 0$, and (under directional convergence of $\mX^T\vr$) $\vbetadiag(\bThetadiag(t))$ aligns with a stationary point of $\min \norms{\vz}_{2/L}$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1$.
conclusions: $\vbetadiag(\bThetadiag(t))$ aligns with stationary point of $\min_{\vz} \norms{\vz}_{2/L}$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1$

nodes.name: Full-length convolutional networks converge to DFT-domain $\ell_{2/L}$ max-margin
nodes.statement: For an $L$-layer linear full-length convolutional network, if $|[\mF\bar\vw_l]_j|^2-|[\mF\bar\vw_L]_j|^2\geq\lambda$ for $l\in[L-1], j\in[d]$, then $\mc L\to 0$ and (under directional convergence of $\mX^T\vr$) $\vbetaconv(\bThetaconv(t))$ aligns with stationary point of $\min \norms{\mF\vz}_{2/L}$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1$.
conclusions: $\vbetaconv(\bThetaconv(t))$ aligns with stationary point of $\min_{\vz} \norms{\mF\vz}_{2/L}$ s.t. $y_i\vx_i^T\vz \geq 1$

nodes.name: Small-filter convolutional networks (single point, $k_1=1,2$)
nodes.statement: For 2-layer linear convolutional networks with single data point $(\vx,y)$: if $k_1=1$ and $\norm{\vx}^2\bar\vv_1^2-(\vx^T\bar\vv_2)^2\geq\norm{\vx}^2\lambda$, then $\vbetaconv$ aligns with $y\vx$. If $k_1=2$ under the analogous gap conditions, $\vbetaconv$ aligns with $2y\vx \pm y\overleftarrow\vx \pm y\overrightarrow\vx$ depending on the sign of the autocorrelation $\vx^T\overleftarrow\vx$.
conclusions: If $k_1=2$: $\vbetaconv$ aligns with low-pass filter $2y\vx + y\overleftarrow\vx + y\overrightarrow\vx$ if $\vx^T\overleftarrow\vx > 0$, high-pass $2y\vx - y\overleftarrow\vx - y\overrightarrow\vx$ if $< 0$

nodes.name: Diagonal networks regression: weighted $\ell_1$/$\ell_2$ interpolation
nodes.statement: For an $L$-layer linear diagonal network with $\bar\vw_l=\bar\vw$ ($l\in[L-1]$), $\bar\vw_L=\zeros$ and $[\bar\vw]_j^2\geq\lambda$, $\vbetadiag(\bThetadiag(t))$ converges to the solution of $\min Q_{L,\alpha,\bar\vw}(\vz)\defeq \alpha^2\sum_j[\bar\vw]_j^2 H_L\big(\frac{[\vz]_j}{\alpha^L|[\bar\vw]_j|^L}\big)$ s.t. $\mX\vz=\vy$.

nodes.name: Convolutional networks regression with even data
nodes.statement: For an $L$-layer linear full-length convolutional network with even data $\vx_i$ and even $\bar\vw$ satisfying $[\mF\bar\vw]_j^2\geq\lambda$, $\vbetaconv(\bThetaconv(t))$ converges to $\vz^\infty$ that solves $\min_{\vz \text{ even}} Q_{L,\alpha,\mF\bar\vw}(\mF\vz)$ s.t. $\mX\vz=\vy$.

nodes.name: Deep matrix sensing recovered as special case
nodes.statement: For depth-$L$ matrix sensing with symmetric commuting $\mA_i$ and initialization $\mW_l(0)=\alpha\mI_d$ for $l\in[L-1]$, $\mW_L(0)=\zeros$, $\mW_1(t)\cdots\mW_L(t)\to \mM^\infty$ minimizing $Q_{L,\alpha}(\eig(\mM))=\alpha^2\sum_j H_L([\eig(\mM)]_j/\alpha^L)$ s.t. $\mc L_{\rm ms}(\mM)=0$.
conclusions: Interpolates between minimum nuclear norm ($\alpha\to 0$) and Frobenius norm ($\alpha\to\infty$) solutions

nodes.name: Directional convergence of homogeneous models (cited)
nodes.statement:
For $L$-homogeneous models with separable data and gradient flow reaching 100\% training accuracy, $
orm{ Theta(t)}	o\infty$, $ Theta(t)/
orm{ Theta(t)}	o Theta^\infty$, and the cosine between $ Theta(t)$ and $-
abla\mc L( Theta(t))$ tends to $1$.

nodes.name: Implicit bias of GD on linear models (cited)
nodes.statement: For linear models $f(\vx;\vz)=\vx^T\vz$ with separable data, GD on exponential loss drives $\norm{\vz}\to\infty$ and $\vz$ converges in direction to the $\ell_2$ max-margin classifier (the solution of \eqref{eq:svm}).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (limit directions are singular vectors)
nodes.statement: Apply the homogeneity-based directional convergence results to the linear tensor network and substitute the gradient-flow ODE to derive the singular-vector relations.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (orthogonally decomposable classification)
nodes.statement: First prove convergence of loss to zero by showing a positive lower bound on a Lyapunov-style gap $|[\mU_l^T\vv_l]_j|^2 - |[\mU_L^T\vv_L]_j|^2$. Then characterize the limit direction using the equivalence to a diagonal network in the $\mU_l^T\vv_l$ coordinates.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (extremely overparameterized classification)
nodes.statement: Convert into a diagonal-network problem in the SVD basis using the single-data-point structure; prove convergence of loss to zero via a gap invariant; identify limit direction with top singular vectors of $\tM(\vx)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4 (orthogonally decomposable regression)
nodes.statement: Reduce to diagonal-network ODEs in the $\mU_l$ basis, characterize limit points as solutions of a constrained minimization of $Q_{L,\alpha,\bar\veta}$ using $h_L$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:ode-real}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5 (single-point regression)
nodes.statement: Solve the gradient-flow ODE explicitly in the SVD basis using $\sinh,\cosh$ substitutions; the residual matches via the implicit equation $g(\nu)=y/\alpha^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6 (fully-connected regression)
nodes.statement: Establish convergence of loss via a Loewner-order monotonicity that propagates through the layers; for the bias part, take limits in $\alpha$ to obtain alignment with the minimum $\ell_2$-norm solution.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (ODE for $h_L$)
nodes.statement: Standard existence/continuity for ODEs gives $p_L,q_L$ on a maximal interval. Compute $\frac{d}{dt}h_L = p_L^{2L-3}(\dots)>0$ to show monotonicity, and analyze blowup at endpoints.

nodes.name: Convergence of loss to zero
nodes.statement: Show that under the gap condition $|[\mU_l^T\bar\vv_l]_j|^2-|[\mU_L^T\bar\vv_L]_j|^2\geq \lambda$, the loss $\mc L(\bTheta(t))$ converges to zero. Uses a Lyapunov-style invariant that the gap is preserved by the gradient flow.

nodes.name: Characterizing the limit direction
nodes.statement: Translating to coordinates $\mU_l^T \vv_l$ reduces the problem to a diagonal network; apply known $\ell_{2/L}$ max-margin results to identify $\vbeta(\bTheta(t))$ as aligning with $\mS^T\vrho^\infty$.

nodes.name: Convergence of loss to zero (single point)
nodes.statement: Use the SVD $\tM(\vx)=\mU_1\diag(\vs)\mU_2^T$ and the gap condition to show that the loss converges to zero in the single-data-point setting.

nodes.name: Characterizing the limit direction (single point)
nodes.statement: Identify $\vv_l$ at infinity with $\mU_l\veta_l^\infty$ where $|\veta_l^\infty|=|\vrho^\infty|^{\odot 1/2}$ for the $\ell_1$ minimizer $\vrho^\infty$ in the singular value space.

nodes.name: Convergence of loss to zero (regression)
nodes.statement: Reduce to diagonal-network coordinates; show that the loss vanishes under the chosen initialization $\bar\vv_l=\mU_l\bar\veta$, $\bar\vv_L=\zeros$, $[\bar\veta]_j^2\geq\lambda$.

nodes.name: Characterizing the limit point via $H_L$
nodes.statement: Express the limit linear coefficient using $h_L$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:ode-real}, integrate to obtain $H_L(t)=\int_0^t h_L^{-1}(\tau) d\tau$, and identify $\vbeta$ as the constrained minimizer of $Q_{L,\alpha,\bar\veta}$.

nodes.name: Convergence of loss to zero (FC regression)
nodes.statement: Use the Loewner-order conditions $\bar\mW_l^T\bar\mW_l \succeq \bar\mW_{l+1}\bar\mW_{l+1}^T$ together with $\bar\mW_{L-1}^T\bar\mW_{L-1}-\bar\vw_L\bar\vw_L^T\succeq\lambda\mI_d$ to propagate a strict lower bound that drives the loss to zero.

nodes.name: Bias to minimum $\ell_2$ norm via $\alpha\to 0$
nodes.statement: Take $\alpha\to 0$ after $t\to\infty$ to show $\vbetafc \to \mX^T(\mX\mX^T)^{-1}\vy$, the minimum $\ell_2$-norm interpolator.

nodes.name: Regression toy experiment with $(\vx,y)=([1\ 2],1)$
nodes.statement: 2-layer linear FC/diagonal/conv networks on a single 2D point. Min-$\ell_2$ solution is $[0.2,0.4]$ (FC), min-$\ell_1$ is $[0,0.5]$ (diagonal), min-DFT-$\ell_1$ is $[0.33,0.33]$ (conv). GD trajectories with $\alpha\in\{0.01,0.5,1\}$ match Theorem~\ref{thm:meta-thm-reg-2} predictions.

nodes.name: Classification toy experiment with two points
nodes.statement: 2-layer linear FC/diagonal/conv networks on $(\vx_1,y_1)=([1\ 2],+1)$, $(\vx_2,y_2)=([0\ -3],-1)$ with $\alpha\in\{0.01,0.5,1\}$ and $T=2\times 10^6$ GD steps. Final coefficients depend on initialization in practice because training does not reach zero loss.

nodes.name: Removal of convergence assumptions
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:meta-thm-clsf-2} extends \citet{gunasekar2018implicit} by removing the directional convergence assumption on parameters and the assumption that loss converges to zero (proven directly under initialization conditions). The directional convergence assumption on $\mX^T\vr$ is not removed.

nodes.name: Necessity of initialization assumptions
nodes.statement: Some initialization conditions are necessary because GD can fail to converge for certain initializations \citep{bartlett2018gradient,arora2019convergence}. The conditions on $\bar\vv_l$ are sufficient (and stronger than $\mc L\to 0$) but checkable a priori, satisfied with probability 1 if $\bar\vv_L=\zeros$ and other $\bar\vv_l$ are random.

nodes.name: Implications to architecture design
nodes.statement: If sparsity under a target linear transform $\mT$ is desired, design a network so that Assumption~\ref{assm:complex-diag-decomp} holds with $\mS=\mT$; gradient flow then biases the solution toward $\mT$-sparse vectors.

nodes.name: Interpolation between $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$
nodes.statement: $H_L(t)$ behaves like $|t|$ for large $|t|$ and like $t^2$ near $0$, so $Q_{L,\alpha,\bar\veta}(\vrho)$ interpolates between weighted $\ell_1$ ($\alpha\to 0$) and weighted $\ell_2$ ($\alpha\to\infty$) norms of $\vrho$.
